samples.summary: The new `merge-paste-partial` integrity guard covers only the internal-paste branch; an external TSV/HTML paste still writes values into cells hidden under a destination merged block, persisting content the user never sees
samples.evidence: `planPasteMerges` is called only inside `if (this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text)` (sheet.ts:2233-2262). The HTML branch (sheet.ts:2287) and the plain-TSV branch (sheet.ts:2291) fall straight through to `setGrid(grid)` (sheet.ts:2303) with `pastedMerges`/`replacedMerges` empty, so cells covered by an existing merge at the destination receive and persist values that render nowhere. The new test at test/sheet/merge.test.ts:561 locks this in ('should leave the merge layout alone on an external paste'). Security-relevant consequence: a user pasting content (possibly sensitive) from Excel/Sheets into a merged region gets no feedback, yet the content is written to the shared CRDT document and is recoverable by any collaborator who unmerges the block, or by an export/xlsx download. The docs record this as a deliberate scope decision (docs/design/sheets/sheet.md, 'External pastes deliberately leave the merge layout alone'), so this is a note on the residual exposure rather than a claim the branch was overlooked — but the guard reads as covering 'paste' when it covers only one of three paste paths.

samples.summary: Internal-paste provenance is decided solely by clipboard-text string equality, and that check now additionally authorizes merge-map mutation (creating merges at the destination, deleting destination merges)
samples.evidence: `if (this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text)` (sheet.ts:2233) is the only provenance test distinguishing an in-app clipboard from foreign clipboard content. Clipboard contents are attacker-influenceable: a web page the user copies from controls the text written to the system clipboard, and a page with clipboard-write permission can plant arbitrary text. Before this change, a collision only triggered formula-reference relocation; now the same equality decides whether `applyPasteMerges` (sheet.ts:2448) deletes destination merged blocks and calls `clearCellsUnderMerge` (sheet.ts:2493), which `store.delete()`s destination cells that the paste did not itself write. Exploitation requires the attacker to know the exact TSV of the victim's last in-app copy, so practical impact is low and confined to destructive edits in the victim's own document — but the widened blast radius argues for a provenance marker (a random buffer id carried in the `text/html` flavour, as Google Sheets does) rather than raw content equality.

samples.summary: No bounds/sanity validation on a `MergeSpan` before it is re-created at the paste destination, so a hostile or corrupted span from the shared CRDT document drives an O(rs*cs) awaited-store-read loop on the victim's paste
samples.evidence: `applyPasteMerges` calls `store.setMerge(merge.anchor, merge.span)` (sheet.ts:2472) and then `clearCellsUnderMerge` (sheet.ts:2493), which iterates every covered sref and performs an `await this.store.get(ref)` per cell (sheet.ts:2506). The span originates from `this.merges`, populated by `loadMerges` (sheet.ts:542-544) straight from `store.getMerges()` with no validation of `rs`/`cs` against sheet dimensions or any cap — `YorkieStore.getMerges` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:1010) just spreads whatever the CRDT root holds, and `merging.ts` only rejects the degenerate `rs<=1 && cs<=1` case. A collaborator with edit rights (or a tampered document) can therefore plant a merge with a huge span and make the victim's copy/paste hang. I could not fully separate this from pre-existing exposure: `rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:816-828) already walks every covered cell of every span at load time, so the same hostile span likely wedges the client before any paste, and `moveRangeTo` already ran the identical per-cell loop. Reported as a hardening gap (validate spans at load/creation), not a new vector.
searchedFor: read loadMerges / getMerges in sheet.ts, store/memory.ts, store/readonly.ts, frontend yorkie-store.ts
grep setMerge|deleteMerge repo-wide for a validating wrapper
